verifications.note: "Iroquois Gas Transmission System, L.P. ... owns and operates a 414-mile interstate natural gas pipeline extending from the U.S.-Canadian border at Waddington, NY ... Since commencing full operations in 1992, Iroquois has continued ..." (present-tense, current operator page).

"Iroquois Gas Transmission System is a 416-mile interstate pipeline jointly owned by a partnership of TC Energy and Berkshire Hathaway. It began operation in 1991 ... It has a physical receipt capability of 1.7 Bcf/d." (Northeast Gas Association member directory, Jul. 2022 edition, describes it in active present tense).

resolutions.researcher_notes: Confirms operating: Iroquois's own current site describes the line in the present tense as an active operated asset, and the (independent, third-party) Northeast Gas Association's 2022 member directory separately describes it as an in-service pipeline with an active receipt capability. No indication anywhere in the harvested material of any shutdown, idling, or decommissioning.

verifications.note: Page titled "Iroquois Gas Transmission System | Canadian Gas Imports"; body: "...interstate natural gas pipeline..."; "Iroquois does not produce the natural gas it carries...we simply transport it...".
"Iroquois Gas Transmission System is a 416-mile interstate pipeline ... It transports natural gas from TC Energy at the Ontario/NY border as well as Marcellus receipts...".

resolutions.researcher_notes: Gas confirmed as a natural gas transmission pipeline by both the operator and the independent trade-association directory.

verifications.note: "Since commencing full operations in 1992, Iroquois has continued to fulfill that promise..." — the operator's own history statement of the in-service year.

"Iroquois System Facilities" fact sheet lists the original Waddington, Canajoharie, Wright and Shelton A interconnects/meter stations all "In-Service Date: December 1991" and the Brookfield interconnect "In-Service Date: November 1992" — construction complete late 1991, full commercial operations 1992, consistent with StartYear1=1992.

resolutions.researcher_notes: 1992 (full operations) is corroborated by the operator's own history page and by its facilities fact sheet's in-service dates for the original interconnects (built out Dec. 1991-Nov. 1992). Note: the TC PipeLines LP archived asset page (already on this row for validity) also states "Began operations 1992", and the Northeast Gas Association's 2022 directory states "began operation in 1991" — read together these describe the same ramp-up (pipe completed/gas flowing late 1991, full commercial operations in 1992), not a conflict.

COULD NOT SOURCE THE RECORDED VALUE (500.00 MMcf/d) — and what I found actively disagrees with it, not just by rounding. TC PipeLines LP's own archived asset page (already on this row, http://web.archive.org/web/20230929001045/https://www.tcpipelineslp.com/assets/iroquois/) states "Capacity 1.5 Bcf/d" (=1,500 MMcf/d), and the Northeast Gas Association's 2022 member directory (https://northeastgas.org/files/galleries/lng_importers0722.pdf) independently states "a physical receipt capability of 1.7 Bcf/d" (=1,700 MMcf/d). Both are ~3x the recorded 500 MMcf/d, well outside any rounding tolerance. Searched: iroquois.com company/history/facilities pages (state length and dates but no capacity figure), iroquois-gas-facts-facilities-list.pdf (compressor-station horsepower only, no throughput figure), rextag.com product page (no capacity figure, only "more than 50% utilization"), EIA naturalgas/data.php (generic portal, no pipeline-specific figure), FERC-EIS URL already on this row (EIS-0152-FEIS-Volume_1_1.pdf) turned out to be the Southeast Market Pipelines (Sabal Trail/Transco/FGT, Florida) EIS — it never mentions Iroquois and cannot be used for this pipeline at all (flagging as a mis-sourced ref already staged on this row for Diameter/Proposal). Two ExC-project seed-citation PDFs (iroquois_exc_project_q_a_02_05_20_web.pdf, exc_brochure.pdf) both 404 on the current site and Wayback's availability API was rate-limiting (429) during this pass, so they were not recoverable to check for a pre/post-ExC capacity figure. 500 MMcf/d may be a stale original-design or pre-expansion figure (Iroquois has undergone several compression/looping expansions since 1992), but no source in hand states 500 specifically — flagging for Update rather than guessing.

verifications.note: "Length 416 miles" = 669.4 km, essentially identical to the recorded 669.00 km (diff <1 km).
"...owns and operates a 414-mile interstate natural gas pipeline..." = 666.3 km.

resolutions.researcher_notes: 669.00 km matches TC PipeLines LP's "416 miles" almost exactly (669.4 km, <1 km / 0.1% off). Iroquois's own site and Rextag (rextag.com, already on this row) both give 414 miles (666.3 km, ~2.7 km / 0.4% off recorded) — a small rounding-level discrepancy between the operator's marketing copy (414 mi) and the co-owner's asset page (416 mi); both are within tolerance of the recorded 669.00 km, no correction needed.

verifications.note: "Waddington Meter Station, Waddington, NY: Point Operator: TCPL ... Interstate Pipeline Interconnect: TransCanada PipeLines" — the pipeline's primary supply-side interconnect is TransCanada's (TC Energy's) Canadian Mainline system at the NY/Ontario border.
"It transports natural gas from TC Energy at the Ontario/NY border as well as Marcellus receipts..." — names the TC Energy Canadian Mainline interconnect as (one of) its gas sources.

resolutions.researcher_notes: "Canadian Mainline" (TransCanada/TC Energy Mainline via the Waddington, NY interconnect) is confirmed as the pipeline's original and still-primary supply interconnect by both the operator's own facilities list and the independent Northeast Gas Association directory. Note the NEGA source shows the source mix has broadened since 1992: Iroquois now also receives Marcellus shale-gas receipts (via its later Wright/Dover-area interconnects with Tennessee Gas and Algonquin), so "Canadian Mainline" remains accurate but is no longer the sole source — worth a mention in ResearcherNotes if this row doesn't already carry it, not a change to FuelSource itself.

verifications.note: "...extending from the U.S.-Canadian border at Waddington, NY, through New York State and western Connecticut to its terminus in Commack, NY, and from Huntington to the Bronx, NY."
"Waddington Meter Station, Waddington, NY" (northern terminus/border interconnect) and "Hunts Point Meter Station, Bronx, NY" (southern terminus) both listed by name.

resolutions.researcher_notes: StartLocation=Waddington, NY and EndLocation=Bronx, NY are both directly confirmed by name in two Iroquois primary-source documents (also independently in the Rextag and TC PipeLines LP pages already on this row: "Originates near: Waddington, New York / Terminates near Hunts Point, Bronx, New York"). FLAGGING A SHEET INCONSISTENCY, not a sourcing problem: the row's StartCountryOrArea is recorded as 'Canada' while StartState/Province is recorded as 'New York' — Waddington, NY is unambiguously on the US side of the border (St. Lawrence County, NY); the Canadian side of this interconnect is near Iroquois, Ontario. StartCountryOrArea='Canada' paired with StartState/Province='New York' is internally inconsistent and looks like a data-entry error worth Update's attention; none of the sources support 'Canada' as the start country for a New York start location.

COULD NOT SOURCE THE RECORDED VALUE ('Iroquois Pipeline Co', 100%) — no source found names a sole owner called 'Iroquois Pipeline Co', and two independent, current sources describe a materially different multi-party ownership structure. Iroquois's own Ownership page (http://www.iroquois.com/company/ownership/, verified 200, name-matched) lists FOUR partners: TC PipeLines, LP (via TC PipeLines GP, Inc.) 49.34%; TransCanada Iroquois LLC (via TransCanada PipeLine USA Ltd.) 0.66%; Iroquois, Inc. (via Eastern Energy Gas Holdings, LLC, a BHE GT&S/Berkshire Hathaway Energy subsidiary) 24.07%; and Iroquois GP Holding Company, LLC (via Iroquois, Inc.) 25.93% -- i.e. ~50% TC Energy affiliates / ~50% Berkshire Hathaway Energy (Dominion Energy Gas legacy) affiliates. Rextag's product page (already on this row) independently corroborates: "Owned by a partnership of TC PipeLines, Berkshire, and TransCanada." Neither names 'Iroquois Pipeline Co' as an owner at all, let alone at 100%. Searched iroquois.com history/facilities pages, the TC PipeLines LP archived asset page (ownership: '49.3% / 0.7% ... TC Energy; 50% ... Dominion Energy, Inc.' -- an older ownership vintage, pre-BHE GT&S rebrand, but still a 4-way split, never a single 100% owner), and Northeast Gas Association's directory ('jointly owned by a partnership of TC Energy and Berkshire Hathaway'). Recommending Update replace the single Owner1='Iroquois Pipeline Co' 100% with the multi-owner split above (exact current percentages per iroquois.com/company/ownership/), rather than staging a ref for a value nothing supports.
